facts.text: Proctorsville was named for Captain Leonard Proctor, a Revolutionary War veteran who moved his family here from Massachusetts in the early 1780s.
Proctorsville is a village located within the town of Cavendish in the Southern Windsor County region of Vermont.
The center of Proctorsville sits along the Black River, just east of the junction of Vermont Route 131 and Route 103.
Proctorsville was founded in the 18th century and was shaped by the development of railroads and the rhythms of nature.
The Dutton and Proctor families of Proctorsville and Duttonsville feuded for seventy-five years until a marriage between the families ended the conflict.
Proctorsville hosts seasonal festivals and immersive storytelling experiences, such as the Murder at Blackwing Hollow event.
